# XPCOM service lookup protects creation, re-entry, and cleanup

## From a JavaScript getter to a shared service

XPCOM is Gecko's component system. A contract ID is the string used to request a registered implementation. `XPCOMUtils.defineLazyServiceGetter()` installs a lazy getter whose callback calls `Cc[aContract].getService(aInterface)`. The request happens on first access, not when the getter is declared.

`GetServiceByContractID()` rejects requests during XPCOM shutdown. Otherwise it takes the component manager monitor, looks up the contract, and passes the entry to `GetServiceLocked()`. Missing registration returns `NS_ERROR_FACTORY_NOT_REGISTERED`.

## Existing and pending services

`GetServiceLocked()` first returns a requested interface from an existing service after releasing the lock. A monitor is the lock and waiting mechanism used to coordinate threads. If another thread is already creating this service, the current thread waits. It checks for an existing instance again after waiting because the other creation may have succeeded or failed.

If the current thread is itself creating the same service, lookup returns `NS_ERROR_NOT_AVAILABLE` instead of recursively constructing it. This prevents a constructor from repeatedly asking for itself.

## Creating without holding the monitor

The method records the pending service, releases the monitor around `CreateInstance()`, and reacquires it afterward. The reason is explicit: constructors run user code that can re-enter the component manager. Holding the monitor through that work could block that re-entry.

On the ordinary success path, it removes the pending entry and wakes waiters, stores the service instance, releases the monitor, and returns a new reference. Factory errors propagate. A factory that reports success without an object has a separate error path.

The scope-exit cleanup releases a retained service only after releasing the monitor. Releasing the last reference can run object destruction code, which can also re-enter other component work. Do not move service destruction under the monitor as a cosmetic cleanup.

## Static entries and overrides

The `GetService(ModuleID, ...)` overload looks up the contract each time when the static entry is overridable. This preserves test overrides. For a non-overridable entry it checks whether the static entry is active.

`RegisterFactory()` can let a dynamic contract override a static contract and invalidate the static lookup. Resetting an existing contract with a null factory has a separate path. These are not equivalent to creating a new instance on every getter access.

This review did not run concurrent-construction tests or prove every exceptional factory path cleans up identically. The claims describe the read branches and explicit source reasons; they are not a full audit of the component manager.

## Evidence and limits

This note describes the code at `1a097ed8d31f6b307a5d0ebc34a82ceaf7f3727b`. Read the named functions with `git show 1a097ed8d31f6b307a5d0ebc34a82ceaf7f3727b:path` in a source clone. Function names are stable anchors; line ranges belong to the accompanying syntax maps. The implementation and named callers were read. No product build or runtime test ran for this study. The note does not prove every branch works, establish a style rule, or explain historical intent beyond reasons stated in the source.
